title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
id_convention: Criterion ids use the policy's own labels: outline numbers joined with dots from the top level (I.A), a heading plus item number for numbered items under an unnumbered heading (Sleep Tests.4), or the section heading for an unnumbered requirement (Initial Coverage). A requirement met by alternatives ('either 1 or 2') is one criterion.
decision_rule: Covered if every applicable criterion for the order is met. Denied if any is not met. Otherwise insufficient information.

E0601.scope: For the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea. A non-OSA diagnosis (e.g. COPD, hypoventilation) falls under the Respiratory Assist Devices LCD (L33800) instead; that is a policy-selection question, not a criterion.

E0470.description: Bi-level respiratory assist device without back-up rate
E0470.scope: For the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea; other diagnoses fall under L33800.

E0471.description: Bi-level respiratory assist device with back-up rate
E0471.scope: Excluded when the primary diagnosis is OSA.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.check: An in-person visit with the treating practitioner, assessing for OSA, dated before the sleep test.
evidence: Procedure or note: sleep apnea assessment during that visit
criteria.notes: Timing matters: a visit after the sleep test does not count. For E0470 after a failed E0601 trial, the original evaluation still counts, but if the E0601 was used for more than 3 months a new in-person evaluation is required (Initial Coverage, paragraphs after II).

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test (as defined below) that meets either of the following criteria (1 or 2): 1. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) or Respiratory Disturbance Index (RDI) is greater than or equal to 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or, 2. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 5 and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of: a. Excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia; or, b. Hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.check: A sleep test (Type I-IV or other home sleep test) with AHI or RDI >= 15 and at least 30 events; or AHI or RDI 5-14 with at least 10 events plus documentation of a symptom or condition from list a or b.
evidence: DiagnosticReport: sleep study, with test type
For AHI 5-14: Condition (hypertension, ischemic heart disease, stroke, insomnia, mood disorder, cognitive impairment) or Observation/note (Epworth score, daytime sleepiness)
criteria.notes: One criterion with two paths. AHI below 5 is not met. AHI 5-14 is met only with a symptom or condition from list a or b (any one is enough), and not met if the record shows neither. The event minimums matter mainly for short recordings: if the AHI or RDI is based on less than 2 hours, the events must still reach 30 (or 10 with symptoms) (Definitions). AHI and RDI exclude RERAs.

criteria.policy_text: A sleep test (Type I, II, III, IV, Other) that meets the Medicare requirements for a valid sleep test as outlined in NCD 240.4.1 and the applicable A/B MAC LCD and Billing and Coding article; and,
criteria.check: The diagnosis rests on a sleep test of a recognized type: a facility-based polysomnogram (Type I) or a home or hospital sleep test (Type II, III, IV, or Other).
evidence: DiagnosticReport: sleep study, stating the test type
criteria.notes: Judged on the test type the record shows. The rest of NCD 240.4.1 (testing standards, billing rules) is administrative and not judged. 'insufficient information' if the record has an AHI but never says what kind of test produced it, even though the policy's definitions imply an AHI comes from a Type I or II study: the type must be stated, not inferred. Wrongly answering 'insufficient' sends the user to find the document; wrongly answering 'met' could approve a claim that should not be.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test results meet the coverage criteria in effect for the date of service of the claim for the PAP device; and,
criteria.check: The sleep test results meet the AHI/RDI criteria (same test as I.B).
criteria.notes: Restates I.B, so its verdict should match I.B. Kept as its own item because the model is likely to judge it separately. A model that leaves it out (having judged I.B) is not penalized; a model that judges it is scored as usual.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner; and,
criteria.check: The sleep test was ordered by the patient's treating practitioner.
criteria.notes: The order itself must be recorded. The treating practitioner discussing the test, or being listed on the test encounter (a sleep physician who runs the test), is not an order: insufficient information.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.check: The patient or caregiver received instruction from the device supplier on how to use and care for the device.
evidence: Procedure or DocumentReference: device education or training
criteria.notes: This is supplier documentation and is often absent from clinical records, so 'insufficient information' will be a common correct answer.

criteria.policy_text: An E0601 has been tried and proven ineffective based on a therapeutic trial conducted in either a facility or in a home setting. Ineffective is defined as documented failure to meet therapeutic goals using an E0601 during the titration portion of a facility-based study or during home use despite optimal therapy (i.e., proper mask selection and fitting and appropriate pressure settings).
criteria.check: A CPAP (E0601) trial, in a facility titration or at home, is documented as failing to meet therapeutic goals despite proper mask fit and pressure settings.
evidence: Device or Procedure: CPAP trial or titration study
Observation or note: failure to meet therapeutic goals
Note: mask fitting and pressure settings were optimized
criteria.notes: E0470 only. Simply having used a CPAP is not enough; the record must show it failed despite optimal therapy. This is the cross-document dependency the project highlights: E0470 depends on an E0601 history. An E0470 ordered at the visit where OSA is first diagnosed, with no CPAP use recorded, is insufficient information: the timeline suggests no trial took place, but the record never says a CPAP wasn't tried elsewhere. Where two readings are defensible, the answer key takes 'insufficient information' (it sends the user to check rather than deciding either way).

criteria.policy_text: A bi-level positive airway pressure device with back-up rate (E0471) is not reasonable and necessary if the primary diagnosis is OSA. If an E0471 is billed with a diagnosis of OSA, it will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
criteria.check: An E0471 is not covered when the primary diagnosis is OSA.
criteria.notes: Unnumbered requirement, so it takes its section heading as its id. 'not met' if the primary diagnosis is OSA. If it is something else, the Respiratory Assist Devices LCD (L33800) governs instead.

continued_coverage.description: Criteria for keeping a PAP device beyond the first 3 months. Applies to a different kind of case than the initial order, so it is kept separate.
continued_coverage.policy_ref: Continued Coverage Beyond the First Three Months of Therapy

criteria.id: Continued Coverage Beyond the First Three Months of Therapy.1
criteria.policy_text: In-person clinical re-evaluation by the treating practitioner with documentation that symptoms of obstructive sleep apnea are improved
criteria.check: An in-person re-evaluation between day 31 and day 91 after starting therapy, documenting improved OSA symptoms.
evidence: Encounter: in-person visit 31-91 days after the device start date
criteria.notes: A re-evaluation after day 91 still qualifies, but coverage restarts from that visit's date.

criteria.id: Continued Coverage Beyond the First Three Months of Therapy.2
criteria.policy_text: Objective evidence of adherence to use of the PAP device, reviewed by the treating practitioner. Adherence to therapy is defined as use of PAP >= 4 hours per night on 70% of nights during a consecutive thirty (30) day period anytime during the first three (3) months of initial usage.
criteria.check: Device usage data showing >= 4 hours per night on at least 70% of nights (21 of 30) in some consecutive 30-day period within the first 3 months, reviewed by the treating practitioner.
evidence: Observation: nightly usage hours or a download summary

out_of_scope.policy_ref: Sleep Tests.2, Sleep Tests.5; General (Standard Written Order, proof of delivery, refills)
out_of_scope.reason: Administrative requirements (device regulatory status, provider qualification, claim documentation) that a clinical record does not show. The judging prompt tells the model to skip this kind of requirement.

out_of_scope.policy_ref: Re-qualifying after a failed 12 week trial; Replacement; Beneficiaries Entering Medicare; Accessories
out_of_scope.reason: Separate claim scenarios. Can be added later as their own checklists if test cases need them.

out_of_scope.policy_ref: Concurrent Use of Oxygen with PAP Therapy
out_of_scope.reason: Requires the Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment LCD (L33797) as well; a good candidate for a later cross-document test case.
